biological.citation: CHAMP1 complex directs heterochromatin assembly and promotes homology-directed DNA repair. (PMID: 39962076)
biological.summary: The CHAMP1 complex (CHAMP1, POGZ, HP1α) promotes heterochromatin assembly at centromeres and telomeres and facilitates homology-directed repair (HDR) of DNA double-strand breaks in these regions. The complex recruits the methyltransferase SETDB1 to heterochromatin. Peripheral blood lymphocytes from individuals with CHAMP1 syndrome exhibit defective heterochromatin clustering and defective DSB repair.

biological.citation: CHAMP1 complex promotes heterochromatin assembly and reduces replication stress. (PMID: 41481470)
biological.summary: Upon replication stress, the CHAMP1 complex (CHAMP1, POGZ, HP1α, SETDB1) is transiently recruited to stalled replication forks, facilitates H3K9me3 deposition, stabilizes forks, and shields them from MRE11-mediated degradation. Loss of the CHAMP1 complex increases micronuclei formation and sensitivity to replication stress, and CHAMP1 deficiency induces synthetic lethality with FANCM inhibition in ALT-positive tumor cells.

biological.citation: CHAMP1 binds to REV7/FANCV and promotes homologous recombination repair. (PMID: 36044844)
biological.summary: CHAMP1 directly binds REV7 via its seatbelt domain, competing with SHLD3, and thereby reduces Shieldin complex levels to increase DSB end resection and activate homologous recombination (HR). CHAMP1 also interacts with POGZ in a heterochromatin complex to further promote HR. In human tumors, CHAMP1 overexpression promotes HR, confers PARP inhibitor resistance, and correlates with poor prognosis.

biological.citation: CHAMP1-POGZ counteracts the inhibitory effect of 53BP1 on homologous recombination and affects PARP inhibitor resistance. (PMID: 35393543)
biological.summary: CHAMP1, in complex with POGZ, promotes DNA end resection by facilitating recruitment of phosphorylated RPA2 and CtIP to DSB sites, thereby promoting HR over NHEJ and counteracting the 53BP1-REV7-Shieldin axis. CHAMP1 depletion suppressed BRCA1 recruitment but not 53BP1 recruitment at DSBs. Loss of CHAMP1 and POGZ restored PARP inhibitor sensitivity in 53BP1/BRCA1-depleted cells.

biological.citation: CHAMP1 premature termination codon mutations found in individuals with intellectual disability cause a homologous recombination defect through haploinsufficiency. (PMID: 39738383)
biological.summary: In EBV-induced lymphoblastoid cells and fibroblasts from individuals with CHAMP1 PTC mutations, truncated CHAMP1 proteins were detected and HR was defective upon DSB induction. In U2OS cells, CHAMP1 PTC mutants could not restore HR when endogenous WT CHAMP1 was depleted, confirming loss-of-function. Heterozygous depletion of CHAMP1 in DLD-1 cells caused an HR defect, demonstrating haploinsufficiency; missense mutants retained HR function.

biological.citation: CHAMP1 is an essential regulator for human myoblast fusion and muscle development. (PMID: 41540007)
biological.summary: CHAMP1 acts as a noncanonical cofactor for the transcription factor MyoD, directly activating expression of the muscle fusogen Myomaker, and is essential for human myoblast fusion both in vitro and in vivo. C2H2-type zinc-finger motifs on CHAMP1 are necessary and sufficient for MyoD interaction and Myomaker expression. Patient-derived cells with CHAMP1 mutations show fusion defects that are fully rescued by restoring Myomaker expression.

biological.citation: Chromosome alignment-maintaining phosphoprotein CHAMP1 plays a role in cell survival through regulating Mcl-1 expression. (PMID: 34107118)
biological.summary: CHAMP1 depletion reduces expression of the anti-apoptotic protein Mcl-1 at both mRNA and protein levels, with CHAMP1 maintaining Mcl-1 stability by suppressing proteasome-dependent degradation independently of cell cycle phase. CHAMP1-depleted cells die earlier during mitotic arrest induced by antimitotic drugs, reducing mitotic slippage. CHAMP1 depletion reduces cell viability and shows synergistic effects with antimitotic drugs.

biological.citation: Dynamic feature of mitotic arrest deficient 2-like protein 2 (MAD2L2) and structural basis for its interaction with chromosome alignment-maintaining phosphoprotein (CAMP). (PMID: 28887307)
biological.summary: Crystal structures of human MAD2L2 (REV7) in complex with a CHAMP1 (CAMP) fragment were determined, revealing that CHAMP1 interacts with MAD2L2 via a novel 'WK' motif with residue interactions distinct from the MAD2L2-REV3 complex. In one crystal form, the MAD2L2-CHAMP1 complex formed a dimer with C-terminal domain swapping, providing evidence for the dynamic nature of MAD2L2 structure. This structural study illuminates the molecular basis for CHAMP1's role in mitosis through MAD2L2 interaction.

biological.citation: De Novo Mutations in CHAMP1 Cause Intellectual Disability with Severe Speech Impairment. (PMID: 26340335)
biological.summary: CHAMP1 encodes a protein with functions in kinetochore-microtubule attachment and regulation of chromosome segregation during mitosis. De novo loss-of-function mutations (frameshift, nonsense) in CHAMP1 were identified in five unrelated individuals with intellectual disability; all mutations are predicted to cause loss of C-terminal zinc-finger domains required for CHAMP1 localization to chromosomes and the mitotic spindle. This established CHAMP1 as a causative gene for intellectual disability.

biological.citation: ASHG 2023 - Characterization of a novel mouse model with 35 bp deletion in Champ1 gene and exploration of AAV gene therapy to correct phenotypic consequences arising from CHAMP1 mutations (T. Carneiro et al.)
biological.summary: A mouse model with a CRISPR/Cas9-induced 35 bp deletion in Champ1 exon 2 (C57BL/6NCrl background) was generated and phenotypically characterized. Heterozygous Champ1 mice exhibit delayed motor development and impairment in memory and learning abilities in behavioral tests. AAV9-mediated delivery of wild-type CHAMP1 is being explored as a gene therapy approach to rescue these phenotypes.
